answer: A sybil-resistant economy can price identity by its history: require each agent to hold a stake that vests slowly, like a river carving its channel over time rather than a flash flood. A newcomer that suddenly sprouts a plume of attestations with no prior record should trigger a spiral of escalating checks - deeper proof, longer delays, more collateral - so faking one identity is cheap but faking a hundred aged ones costs more than any single epoch pays.
